title: Binary Cross-Entropy
statement: Implement `bce(y_true, y_prob)`, the mean binary cross-entropy. Labels are 0 or 1 and probabilities are in (0, 1). Clip each probability into the closed range 1e-12 through 1 − 1e-12 before the log, then average −(y log p + (1 − y) log(1 − p)) over the batch.
constraints: Return the mean, not the sum

approaches.name: Clipped mean NLL
approaches.explanation: BCE is the negative log likelihood of independent Bernoulli trials.

editorial: Binary cross-entropy is the negative log likelihood under a Bernoulli model. It punishes confident wrong answers much harder than squared error on probabilities, which is why classifiers train with log loss. Clipping keeps the log defined when a model emits an exact 0 or 1. With a sigmoid output, the gradient of BCE with respect to the logit collapses to p − y, a fact interviewers love.
